name: RPM / DNF
client: DNF and RPM bundled with Fedora 44 (immutable image)
auth: Use an access or reference token as the HTTP Basic password, with AW_USER equal to its subject. The subject needs read permission for installation and deploy permission for publication on the selected repository; token scopes cannot exceed that identity. The same clients also accept a user password when Basic password authentication is enabled. Use HTTPS.
fresh_home: Create a new AW_WORK with mktemp -d for every run; client configuration, downloads and caches in the commands stay under this directory. Do not reuse it to prove a fresh download. Remove the temporary directory after use.
prerequisites: Run as root inside a fresh Fedora container, never against the host package database.
Signed repodata and its trusted GPG key; this command is not for an unsigned feed.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/home"
AW_AUTH_URL=$(python3 - <<'PYCODE'
import os
from urllib.parse import quote, urlsplit, urlunsplit
u = urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"])
auth = quote(os.environ["AW_USER"], safe="") + ":" + quote(os.environ["AW_TOKEN"], safe="")
print(urlunsplit((u.scheme, auth + "@" + u.netloc, u.path, "", "")))
PYCODE
)
mkdir -p "$AW_WORK/root" "$AW_WORK/cache"
cp "$AW_SIGNING_PUBLIC_KEY" "$AW_WORK/rpm-sign.pub"
configure.note: Run in a fresh Fedora container as root. Verify the repository signing key with the operator first; Python 3 is used for URL encoding.

publish.note: Publish to a local or one-node federated repository. Remote repositories are read-through caches; select the local deployment member when reading through a virtual.

steps.note: Enable calculateYumMetadata on the repository, or have an authorized operator run metadata calculation.

install.note: Select a local, remote, virtual or one-node federated repository with read permission. Dependencies must also be available through that repository.

steps.note: This reproduces the signed-metadata fixture: metadata signatures and package hashes are verified, but the fixture RPM is not package-signed. For package-signed production RPMs, configure package signing trust and enable gpgcheck.

limitations: Example package matches the existing controlled fixture. Repository metadata signature verification and RPM package signature verification are distinct.
Virtual metadata signing requires a key on the virtual repository.
